method: Static reverse engineering, rizin and bounded Unicorn decompression; no sample or npm lifecycle code executed.

evidence: UPX checksum fails; emulated entry 0x428610 through 0x428716 to recover code and undo the E8/E9 filter without invoking Windows APIs. Stub hands control to 0x401130, CRT to 0x401020, then main 0x4013a0.

Main obtains its own path (0x4013ce), opens rb (0x4013da), reads the complete executable into a buffer (0x40142c), searches for a mutation slot (0x401470-0x40149e), waits 30000ms (0x4014e1), randomizes sixteen bytes (0x401551-0x40155e), writes a randomly named copy (0x40156b-0x401599), and posts multipart file[], node and submit fields using libcurl (0x4015e1-0x401656). Node choice is rand()%7+1.

No arbitrary-file harvesting, command dispatch, victim discovery, startup registration, defender changes or attacker-selected execution sink found. The upload is self-submission; its response is not interpreted as code or tasking.

Offset 85131 holds an unreferenced truncated PE with a custom decoder and CLR identifiers. It lacks its complete import/resource data. The recovered host reads the overlay as part of its complete self-image and copies/uploads it, but has no path that maps, extracts or executes it. Initializers contain no added constructor.

Host compact UPX import names include GetModuleFileNameA, GetModuleHandleA, LoadLibraryA, VirtualProtect and CRT allocation. No CreateProcess, ShellExecute, executable-memory allocation or resource activation import is present in the recovered host.
samples.source_label_explanation: Continuous executable mutation and remote self-submission resemble a worm and trigger reputation/signature rules. The node-specific Wecan destination was an executable-submission playground; no independent hostile operation was established. The appended protected-code fragment supplies additional misleading malware signatures.

url_check.observed: 301 to HTTPS, then redirect to ipv4.games/claim?name=CollabVM; returned a small HTML claim page. No executable response or secondary payload. GET only; no sample uploaded by the review.

evidence: CRT entry 0x4014e0 reaches main 0x461b50. Main creates a Lua state (0x41a0a0), calls pmain 0x4021a0 through protected Lua execution (0x40c3a0), reports errors, closes state and exits.

pmain parses -e/-l/-j/-O/-i/-v/-E arguments, initializes libraries, handles LUA_INIT unless environment use is disabled, then runs requested scripts or stdin/REPL. Compared with upstream src/luajit.c; a behavior comparison, not a byte-identical build claim.
TLS callbacks 0x45ee50 and 0x45ee00 dispatch MinGW TLS initialization/cleanup to 0x45f750, including critical sections and runtime thread bookkeeping. No payload handoff found.

VirtualAlloc/VirtualProtect implement JIT code and FFI support. The PE-header walk is MinGW image-section introspection, not a reflective payload loader. The apparent GetPC match combined unrelated instruction bytes, not call-next/pop.

Only ordinary KERNEL32/msvcrt imports and a manifest resource are present. The overlay holds COFF symbols; no malicious Lua program, embedded malicious bytecode, downloader, network endpoint or injected startup path found.
samples.source_label_explanation: The sole engine explicitly labels MisusedLegit.LuaJIT. A legitimate standalone interpreter is routinely bundled beside malicious scripts; this supplied file provides the interpreter only. Reputation of a surrounding campaign does not establish hostile behavior in this executable.

url_check.observed: Official LuaJIT project page; upstream LuaJIT v2.1 src/luajit.c and lj_clib.c fetched and inspected.

evidence: scripts/postinstall.mjs exits in CI, otherwise prints setup instructions and exits. No import of a runtime writer, no network, no process launch and no instruction-file modification occurs on this hook path.

dist/core/host-exports/export.js runs through explicit CLI provisioning, checks host roots, skips help/version, protects markerless user files and exports generated slash commands. dist/builtin-pi-packages/pi-crtr-extensions/lib/subscription-state.ts reads/writes provider auth and rotation state. Pooling these with the separate install manifest did not prove install-time injection.
dist/core/self-update.js imports fetch from ./git.js; fetch(mkt.root,mkt.ref) is Git remote-reference maintenance, not an inbound WebSocket HTTP request.

Minified attach bundle includes ordinary LRU cache eviction, Google application-default credential handling, file-search tools, model providers and child-process support. Split/join normalizes paths. Browser assets are minified UI builds, not an encoded payload dispatcher.

The impersonation phrase occurs in a comment saying cancellation must NOT masquerade as a human result. Always-respond wording is an HTTP-error handling comment, not an instruction to an LLM. p.kind === flag filters CLI parameters, not sensitive filenames.

Control-plane relaying is session/registry-gated and derives upstream authority from the selected home. OAuth/model credentials go to the configured provider/home. No hidden credential-export destination or attacker command path found.

Bootstrap clones the disclosed official marketplace and registers it without enabling plugins. Referenced Google GitHub repository HTML brought in GitHub behavior/code-view assets during scanner following; those assets implement normal DOM/UI fetches and have no npm install execution path.

Humanloop dependency provisions its pinned termrender rendering venv with uv. The printed curl-to-uv command is advice when uv is absent. Reviewed downloaded termrender code uses terminal/document rendering and optional tmux subprocesses; no concealed export path found.
samples.source_label_explanation: Socket leads include an install hook, young/rapid release metadata, bundled agent execution tools, auth handling and substantial minified code. These capabilities fit its disclosed agent-orchestrator purpose; the suspicious rule incorrectly joined independent archive members.
samples.dependency_review: Downloaded the declared minimum versions of 31/32 direct dependencies, plus fetched applicable resolved Humanloop/pi versions and GitHub UI assets. tw-animate-css 1.0.0 returned 404; its currently available 1.4.0 distribution was retrieved as a separately identified fallback. This does not reconstruct an exact historical unlocked dependency graph.

intentional_match_changes: Replace broad pushad/any-call/pop GetPC byte pattern with a call to the immediately following pop EBP, preserving the entry/.text bounds. No malicious intent inferred from the instruction idiom.
Filename flag observation requires filename/path wording; generic filter is insufficient because it matches CLI parameter metadata.
Remove duplicate Google credential-read alias in objectives and reference the canonical neutral credential-env read.
Relocate unproven postinstall/writer co-occurrence to a notable filesystem context. It does not assert hook reachability.
Keep LoadLibraryExA notable in recognized runtimes and remove the unsupported DLL-hijack ATT&CK mapping.
Rename executable-memory-staging to describe page constants/protection arguments without asserting staging.

Retain suspicious coverage for a module-level instruction-file write beside global agent scope, without inferring install-hook reachability. The direct-write hostile fixture now requires this evidence.

directory_consumers.socket/init: SwiftTunnel UDP relay selector also references the moved bind observation, retaining its former member coverage.
directory_consumers.embedded/payload/header: XZ selector is scoped to ELF; the relocated e_lfanew pattern is PE/DLL-only and could not satisfy that consumer.

limitations: Analysis is static; no Windows live execution was performed.
Dead/truncated overlay data does not prove its original complete protected application purpose.
A floating npm dependency declaration does not fix one historical installation graph; unavailable/fallback versions are recorded explicitly.
